public_rationale: The rejection of universal locked-in demand holds for the planned buildout: IREN explicitly said its deployment-based revenue target was not fully contracted. The restriction to named buyers does not hold under the ordinary contractual reading: Jane Street had announced a substantial AI-cloud commitment. This result depends on reading guaranteed as committed customer demand. The disclosures do not establish that any contract is immune to default or termination.
limitations: Support concerns planned deployments, not an assertion that IREN's operational capacity was uncontracted.
The customer counterexample establishes an announced agreement, not unconditional credit protection.
A stricter interpretation of guaranteed would leave the exclusivity component unresolved.

Treat the named-customer restriction as a claim about publicly documented commitments, not a claim about what Zitron personally searched.

criteria.support_condition: A disclosed planned AI deployment lacks full customer commitments, supporting the rejection of universal coverage. Support for the customer restriction additionally requires evidence that qualifying commitments are confined to the named buyers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A disclosed AI-capacity agreement with an established customer outside the named group contradicts the customer restriction. Evidence that all relevant deployments were fully committed would contradict the first component.
